chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Ash'ari, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from al-Washa', from al-Mufaddal ibn Salih, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

He said to me: 'Let those who are behind the Imam be the men of understanding and intelligence among you. So if the Imam forgets or becomes tired, they should correct him. And the best of the rows is the first one, and the best of the first row is that which is nearest to the Imam. And the superiority of the congregational prayer over the prayer of a lone man is twenty-five degrees in Paradise.'
ai.seo_question: What is the reward of congregational prayer compared to individual prayer in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the collaborative nature of leadership in Shia tradition, where 'ulī al-ḥilm' (men of understanding) assist the Imam, reflecting the concept of shared responsibility in religious authority. It further establishes the merit of congregational prayer by linking physical proximity to the Imam with spiritual excellence, quantifying the reward as twenty-five degrees above individual prayer. This underscores the communal aspect of worship and the Imam's central role in guiding the faithful both spiritually and ritually.

en.hubeali:
Al Husayn Bin Muhammad Al Ashary, from Moalla Bin Muhammad, from Al Washa, from Al Mufazzal Bin Salih, from Jabir, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Let those who are behind the Imam be the most forbearing and intelligent of you. So if the Imam were to forget or get tired, they can straighten (correct) him; and the most superior of the rows is its first one, and the most superior of it is what is nearest to the Imam, and the superiority of the Jam’atal Salāt over the Salāt of the lone man is twenty five Levels in the Paradise’.
en.sarwar: 7. Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Ash’ariy from Mu‘alla’ ibn Muhammad from al-Washsha’ from al-Mufaddal ibn Salih from Jabir who has said the following: “Abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has sad, ‘

Those of you who are just behind the Imam are people of forbearance and wisdom, so that if Imam forgets or becomes tired they can help. The excellent row is the first row and excellent in the first row is the place nearest to the Imam. The height of the excellence of Salah (prayer) in congregation over Salah (prayer) of a man alone is twenty-five degrees in paradise.’”
